args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

The docstring claimed banker's rounding but the implementation used
ROUND_HALF_UP. Import and apply ROUND_HALF_EVEN so half-cent values
round to the nearest even cent, as required by FIN-212 and expected
by tests/test_money.py.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
`src/money.py` claimed to implement banker's rounding (per FIN-212) but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, causing the nightly build failure in `tests/test_money.py`.

## Changes
- Import `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `src/money.py`.
- Quantize with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` so half-cent values round to the nearest even cent (e.g. `2.675 → 2.68`, `2.665 → 2.66`).

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch (commit 08d3cd5986) passed, including `tests/test_money.py`.

Fixes the nightly build failure for FIN-212.

2. Committed the fix: changed the import and `quantize` rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
3. Triggered CI — the run (`ci-0001`) **passed** on commit `08d3cd5986` (an early status lookup briefly showed a flaky unrelated failure on main itself, but the branch run is green).
4. Opened PR #101 against main: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101, with alex requested as reviewer.

Per policy, I did not merge — it awaits alex's/code owner review and approval.
